# Goal

Test whether symbiont composition changed across sampling eras while accounting
for uneven sampling depth among eras.

This cleaned analysis uses post-MED ITS2 sequence variants only. Type profiles,
exploratory maps, old commented code, and temporary one-off exports were removed.
The working composition scale is symbiont clade/genus: `A`, `B`, `C`, `D`, and
`G`.

# Required input files

Copy these files from the previous project into the paths below.

```{r required-files}
required_files
```

```{r check-input-files}
missing_files <- required_files |>
  filter(!file.exists(path))

if (nrow(missing_files) > 0) {
  knitr::kable(missing_files, caption = "Files still needed before the analysis can run.")
  knitr::knit_exit()
}
```

# Load and clean data

```{r load-data}
metadata <- load_sample_metadata("metadata/decadalshifts_SST.xls")

variant_runs <- load_variant_runs(c(
  pawar = required_files$path[required_files$key == "pawar_variants"],
  conn = required_files$path[required_files$key == "conn_variants"]
))

sample_clades <- prepare_sample_clade_composition(
  metadata = metadata,
  variants = variant_runs,
  min_reads = 100
)

sample_retention <- audit_sample_retention(
  metadata = metadata,
  variants = variant_runs,
  min_reads = 100
)

readr::write_csv(sample_clades, "data/processed/sample_clade_composition.csv")
readr::write_csv(sample_retention$stage_counts, "outputs/tables/sample_retention_audit.csv")
readr::write_csv(sample_retention$dropped_samples, "outputs/tables/dropped_samples.csv")
```

## Summarize samples by era

Visualize the retained samples across collection subregions, host species, and
sampling eras before any species-group filtering.

```{r sample-summary-by-era}
sample_summary <- sample_clades |>
  count(collection_subregion, host_species_code, era, name = "n") |>
  arrange(collection_subregion, host_species_code, era)

plot_sample_count_heatmap <- function(summary_df, title, subtitle) {
  species_order <- summary_df |>
    group_by(host_species_code) |>
    summarize(total = sum(n), .groups = "drop") |>
    arrange(total) |>
    pull(host_species_code)

  summary_df |>
    mutate(
      era = factor(era, levels = eras),
      host_species_code = factor(host_species_code, levels = species_order)
    ) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = era, y = host_species_code, fill = n)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_text(aes(label = n), size = 3) +
    facet_wrap(~ collection_subregion, nrow = 1) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f7f7f2", high = "#2a6f97", name = "Samples") +
    labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = "Host species",
      fill = "Samples",
      title = title,
      subtitle = subtitle
    ) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      strip.background = element_blank(),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
      panel.spacing.x = unit(1.2, "lines"),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1),
      axis.ticks = element_blank(),
      panel.grid = element_blank()
    )
}

plot_sample_count_heatmap(
  sample_summary,
  title = "ITS2 samples retained for analysis",
  subtitle = "Counts by collection subregion, host species, and sampling era"
)
```

## Filter analysis groups

Keep only subregion-by-species groups with enough samples for era comparisons:
at least `sample_filter_min_total` total samples and at least
`sample_filter_min_eras` eras with `sample_filter_min_n` samples.

```{r filter-analysis-groups}
sample_filter_min_n <- 2
sample_filter_min_eras <- 2
sample_filter_min_total <- 11

sample_group_filter <- sample_summary |>
  group_by(collection_subregion, host_species_code) |>
  summarize(
    total_n = sum(n),
    eras_at_min_n = sum(n >= sample_filter_min_n),
    retained = total_n >= sample_filter_min_total & eras_at_min_n >= sample_filter_min_eras,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

sample_filter_audit <- sample_group_filter |>
  count(collection_subregion, retained, name = "n_species_groups")

knitr::kable(
  sample_filter_audit,
  caption = paste(
    "Species groups retained with total n >=",
    sample_filter_min_total,
    "and at least",
    sample_filter_min_eras,
    "eras with n >=",
    sample_filter_min_n
  )
)

retained_sample_groups <- sample_group_filter |>
  filter(retained) |>
  select(collection_subregion, host_species_code)

sample_summary_retained <- sample_summary |>
  semi_join(retained_sample_groups, by = c("collection_subregion", "host_species_code"))

plot_sample_count_heatmap(
  sample_summary_retained,
  title = "ITS2 samples retained after species-group filtering",
  subtitle = paste(
    "Keeping subregion-species groups with total n >=",
    sample_filter_min_total,
    "and at least",
    sample_filter_min_eras,
    "eras with n >=",
    sample_filter_min_n
  )
)
```

## Harmonize collection site names

Create a harmonized site-name variable before site-level diagnostics. Current
manual rules only modify Upper Keys names; other subregions retain their raw
site names.

```{r harmonize-site-names}
sample_clades_retained <- sample_clades |>
  semi_join(retained_sample_groups, by = c("collection_subregion", "host_species_code")) |>
  mutate(
    collection_site_harmonized = case_when(
      collection_subregion == "Upper Keys" &
        str_detect(str_to_lower(collection_site), "cheeca") ~ "Cheeca Rocks",
      collection_subregion == "Upper Keys" &
        str_detect(str_to_lower(collection_site), "outer reef") ~ "Outer Reef",
      collection_subregion == "Upper Keys" &
        str_to_lower(collection_site) %in% c("conch", "conch reef") ~ "Conch",
      collection_subregion == "Upper Keys" &
        collection_site %in% c("Hens and Chickens", "Tavernier Rocks") ~ "Tavernier Rocks",
      TRUE ~ collection_site
    )
  )
```

## Summarize retained sites

Break the filtered samples down by harmonized collection site, host species,
and sampling era. Within each site, era slots are ordered left-to-right as
`2001-03`, `2019-21`, and `2024`.

```{r site-species-era-summary}
site_species_summary <- sample_clades_retained |>
  filter(!is.na(collection_site_harmonized), !is.na(era)) |>
  count(
    collection_subregion, collection_site_harmonized,
    host_species_code, era,
    name = "n_samples"
  )

plot_site_species_heatmap <- function(summary_df, subregion) {
  subregion_df <- summary_df |>
    filter(collection_subregion == subregion)

  site_positions <- subregion_df |>
    group_by(collection_site_harmonized) |>
    summarize(
      site_n = sum(n_samples),
      n_2024 = sum(if_else(era == "2024", n_samples, 0L)),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    arrange(desc(n_2024), desc(site_n), collection_site_harmonized) |>
    mutate(site_index = row_number())

  species_positions <- subregion_df |>
    group_by(host_species_code) |>
    summarize(species_n = sum(n_samples), .groups = "drop") |>
    arrange(species_n) |>
    mutate(species_y = row_number())

  era_offsets <- tibble(
    era = factor(eras, levels = eras),
    era_offset = c(-0.26, 0, 0.26)
  )

  plot_df <- subregion_df |>
    left_join(site_positions, by = "collection_site_harmonized") |>
    left_join(species_positions, by = "host_species_code") |>
    left_join(era_offsets, by = "era") |>
    mutate(x = site_index + era_offset)

  site_breaks <- site_positions |>
    filter(site_index < max(site_index)) |>
    mutate(xintercept = site_index + 0.5)

  ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = x, y = species_y, fill = n_samples)) +
    geom_vline(
      data = site_breaks,
      aes(xintercept = xintercept),
      color = "grey84",
      linewidth = 0.25
    ) +
    geom_tile(width = 0.24, height = 0.78, color = "white", linewidth = 0.35) +
    geom_text(aes(label = n_samples), size = 3) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = site_positions$site_index,
      labels = site_positions$collection_site_harmonized,
      expand = expansion(add = 0.7)
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      breaks = species_positions$species_y,
      labels = species_positions$host_species_code,
      expand = expansion(add = 0.6)
    ) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f7f7f2", high = "#2a6f97", name = "Samples") +
    labs(
      x = "Harmonized collection site (left to right within site: 2001-03, 2019-21, 2024)",
      y = "Host species",
      title = paste("Filtered", subregion, "samples by harmonized site"),
      subtitle = "Each site has one x-axis label and fixed three-era slots"
    ) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
      axis.ticks = element_blank(),
      panel.grid = element_blank()
    )
}

plot_site_species_heatmap(site_species_summary, "Dry Tortugas")
plot_site_species_heatmap(site_species_summary, "Upper Keys")
```

# Sampling depth diagnostics

Summarize depth distributions by harmonized collection site, host species, and
era to check whether cross-era comparisons are being driven by site-level depth
differences.

```{r depth-diagnostics}
depth_summary <- sample_clades_retained |>
  group_by(
    collection_subregion, collection_site_harmonized,
    host_species_code, era
  ) |>
  summarize(
    n = n(),
    n_depth = sum(!is.na(depth_ft)),
    median_depth_ft = median(depth_ft, na.rm = TRUE),
    q25_depth_ft = quantile(depth_ft, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q75_depth_ft = quantile(depth_ft, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    across(
      c(median_depth_ft, q25_depth_ft, q75_depth_ft),
      ~ if_else(is.nan(.x), NA_real_, .x)
    )
  )

readr::write_csv(depth_summary, "outputs/tables/depth_summary_by_harmonized_site_era.csv")

site_depth_order <- depth_summary |>
  group_by(collection_subregion, collection_site_harmonized) |>
  summarize(
    site_n = sum(n),
    median_site_depth_ft = median(median_depth_ft, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(collection_subregion, median_site_depth_ft, collection_site_harmonized) |>
  pull(collection_site_harmonized) |>
  unique()

depth_summary_plot <- depth_summary |>
  mutate(
    collection_site_harmonized = factor(collection_site_harmonized, levels = site_depth_order),
    site_plot_label = str_trunc(as.character(collection_site_harmonized), width = 36),
    site_plot_label = factor(site_plot_label, levels = str_trunc(site_depth_order, width = 36)),
    era = factor(era, levels = eras),
    depth_label = if_else(n_depth > 0, as.character(n), paste0(n, "*"))
  )

ggplot(depth_summary_plot, aes(x = era, y = site_plot_label)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = median_depth_ft), color = "white", linewidth = 0.35) +
  geom_text(aes(label = depth_label), size = 2.6) +
  facet_grid(
    collection_subregion ~ host_species_code,
    scales = "free_y",
    space = "free_y"
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "C",
    na.value = "grey90",
    name = "Median depth (ft)"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Harmonized collection site",
    caption = "Tile labels are sample counts; an asterisk marks rows with no usable depth values."
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7),
    axis.ticks = element_blank()
  )

ggsave("outputs/figures/depth_by_harmonized_site_era.png", width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 300)
```

# Symbiont composition

For each subregion-by-species group, samples are weighted so each era better
matches the pooled distribution of harmonized collection sites and, where
available, pooled depth bins. This preserves the observed samples while reducing
bias from eras being sampled at different sites or depths.

Dry Tortugas samples are site-standardized but not depth-standardized because
one era lacks depth information. Other subregion-by-species groups without
usable depth information are also retained and standardized only by the
available design variables.

Groups with fewer than `min_n` samples in an era are retained with `NA`
composition for that era rather than silently dropped.

```{r standardized-composition}
min_n <- sample_filter_min_n

composition_std <- standardized_era_composition(
  sample_clades_retained,
  min_n = min_n,
  n_bins = 6,
  no_depth_standardization_subregions = "Dry Tortugas"
)

standardization_targets <- standardization_target_distribution(
  sample_clades_retained,
  composition = composition_std,
  n_bins = 6,
  no_depth_standardization_subregions = "Dry Tortugas"
)

standardization_target_margins <- bind_rows(
  standardization_targets |>
    filter(!is.na(collection_site_harmonized)) |>
    summarize(
      n_target = sum(n_target),
      target_total_n = first(target_total_n),
      target_proportion = sum(target_proportion),
      target_percent = 100 * target_proportion,
      .by = c(collection_subregion, host_species_code, standardization_method, collection_site_harmonized)
    ) |>
    transmute(
      collection_subregion, host_species_code, standardization_method,
      target_variable = "site",
      target_level = collection_site_harmonized,
      n_target, target_total_n, target_proportion, target_percent
    ),
  standardization_targets |>
    filter(!is.na(depth_bin)) |>
    summarize(
      n_target = sum(n_target),
      target_total_n = first(target_total_n),
      target_proportion = sum(target_proportion),
      target_percent = 100 * target_proportion,
      .by = c(collection_subregion, host_species_code, standardization_method, depth_bin)
    ) |>
    transmute(
      collection_subregion, host_species_code, standardization_method,
      target_variable = "depth_bin",
      target_level = depth_bin,
      n_target, target_total_n, target_proportion, target_percent
    )
) |>
  arrange(collection_subregion, host_species_code, target_variable, desc(target_proportion), target_level)

era_distances <- compare_eras(composition_std)

across_region_composition <- combine_regions_by_species(
  composition_std,
  regions = c("Upper Keys", "Dry Tortugas"),
  region_weighting = "equal"
)

across_region_distances <- compare_eras_by_species(across_region_composition)

readr::write_csv(composition_std, "data/processed/site_depth_standardized_composition.csv")
readr::write_csv(standardization_targets, "outputs/tables/composition_standardization_targets.csv")
readr::write_csv(
  standardization_target_margins,
  "outputs/tables/composition_standardization_target_margins.csv"
)
readr::write_csv(era_distances, "outputs/tables/era_composition_distances.csv")
readr::write_csv(
  across_region_composition,
  "data/processed/across_region_species_composition.csv"
)
readr::write_csv(
  across_region_distances,
  "outputs/tables/across_region_species_era_distances.csv"
)
```

```{r composition-plot}
composition_long <- composition_std |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(clades), names_to = "clade", values_to = "proportion") |>
  filter(!is.na(proportion))

ggplot(composition_long, aes(x = era, y = proportion, fill = clade)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8, color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  facet_grid(collection_subregion + standardization_method ~ host_species_code) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Symbiont composition", fill = "Clade") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1))

ggsave("outputs/figures/site_depth_standardized_composition.png", width = 13, height = 7, dpi = 300)
```

# Statistical test

The primary test is a PERMANOVA on clade composition within each
subregion-by-species group. Era is evaluated after available design terms, so
groups with site and depth structure are tested as:

`composition ~ depth_bin + site + era`

Groups without usable depth data are kept and tested as:

`composition ~ site + era`

These tests are paired with the composition summaries above so the biological
effect sizes are interpretable.

```{r permanova}
permanova_results <- permanova_by_group(
  sample_clades_retained,
  min_n = min_n,
  permutations = 999,
  no_depth_adjustment_subregions = "Dry Tortugas"
)

readr::write_csv(permanova_results, "outputs/tables/permanova_by_subregion_species.csv")

format_p <- function(p) {
  case_when(
    is.na(p) ~ "",
    p < 0.001 ~ "&lt;0.001***",
    p < 0.01 ~ sprintf("%.3f**", p),
    p < 0.05 ~ sprintf("%.3f*", p),
    TRUE ~ sprintf("%.3f", p)
  )
}

format_sig_p <- function(p) {
  formatted <- format_p(p)
  if_else(!is.na(p) & p < 0.05, paste0("<strong>", formatted, "</strong>"), formatted)
}

permanova_results |>
  arrange(host_species_code, collection_subregion) |>
  select(-site_adjusted, -depth_adjusted) |>
  mutate(
    p_depth_bin = format_sig_p(p_depth_bin),
    p_site = format_sig_p(p_site),
    p_era = format_sig_p(p_era)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(escape = FALSE)
```

## Site/depth-standardized composition shifts

Summarize pairwise era shifts using Hellinger distances calculated from the
site/depth-standardized composition estimates above. Points include
subregion-specific shifts and a species-level field summary that averages
available subregions equally when more than one subregion is available.

```{r standardized-shift-plot}
standardized_shift_plot_data <- bind_rows(
  era_distances |>
    filter(!is.na(Hellinger)) |>
    transmute(
      field_scale = collection_subregion,
      host_species_code,
      era1, era2,
      Hellinger
    ),
  across_region_distances |>
    filter(!is.na(Hellinger)) |>
    transmute(
      field_scale = "Species-level",
      host_species_code,
      era1, era2,
      Hellinger
    )
) |>
  mutate(
    contrast = factor(
      paste(era1, "to", era2),
      levels = c("2001-03 to 2019-21", "2019-21 to 2024", "2001-03 to 2024")
    ),
    field_scale = factor(
      field_scale,
      levels = c("Species-level", "Upper Keys", "Dry Tortugas")
    )
  )

standardized_shift_species_order <- standardized_shift_plot_data |>
  summarize(max_hellinger = max(Hellinger), .by = host_species_code) |>
  arrange(desc(max_hellinger)) |>
  pull(host_species_code)

standardized_shift_plot_data <- standardized_shift_plot_data |>
  mutate(
    host_species_code = factor(host_species_code, levels = standardized_shift_species_order)
  )

standardized_shift_plot <- ggplot(
  standardized_shift_plot_data,
  aes(x = host_species_code, y = Hellinger, color = contrast, shape = field_scale)
) +
  geom_point(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.55),
    size = 2.8,
    alpha = 0.85
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.06))) +
  labs(
    x = "Host species",
    y = "Hellinger distance",
    color = "Era contrast",
    shape = "Field scale",
    title = "Site/depth-standardized symbiont composition shifts",
    subtitle = "Species-level points weight available subregions equally; single-region species collapse to that region"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

standardized_shift_plot

ggsave("outputs/figures/site_depth_standardized_hellinger_shifts_by_species.png", standardized_shift_plot, width = 11, height = 6.5, dpi = 300)
```

# Field-observed composition take-homes

Before comparing field shifts to experimental shuffling, the table and figure
below summarize the field observations on their own. These species-level values
use the same standardized composition estimates as above: Upper Keys estimates
are standardized across site and depth, Dry Tortugas estimates are standardized
across site, and species with both subregions available are averaged across
subregions equally.

```{r field-observed-shift-summary}
field_observed_shift_summary <- across_region_composition |>
  filter(era %in% c("2019-21", "2024")) |>
  mutate(era_key = if_else(era == "2019-21", "era_2019_21", "era_2024")) |>
  select(
    host_species_code,
    era_key,
    n_total,
    n_regions,
    regions_included,
    durusdinium = D
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = era_key,
    values_from = c(durusdinium, n_total, n_regions, regions_included),
    names_sep = "__"
  ) |>
  left_join(
    across_region_distances |>
      filter(era1 == "2019-21", era2 == "2024") |>
      select(host_species_code, hellinger_2019_21_to_2024 = Hellinger),
    by = "host_species_code"
  ) |>
  filter(
    !is.na(durusdinium__era_2019_21),
    !is.na(durusdinium__era_2024)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    durusdinium_change = durusdinium__era_2024 - durusdinium__era_2019_21
  )

field_observed_species_labels <- function(flags) {
  species <- field_observed_shift_summary$host_species_code[flags]
  if (length(species) == 0) {
    "None"
  } else {
    paste(sort(species), collapse = ", ")
  }
}

field_observed_metric_table <- tibble(
  `Field-observed summary` = c(
    "2024 Durusdinium >= 50%",
    "2024 Durusdinium >= 75%",
    "2024 Durusdinium >= 90%",
    "Increase >= 25 percentage points from 2019-21 to 2024",
    "Increase >= 50 percentage points from 2019-21 to 2024",
    "Shift from <25% to >=50% Durusdinium",
    "Whole-community Hellinger distance >= 0.5"
  ),
  n_species = c(
    sum(field_observed_shift_summary$durusdinium__era_2024 >= 0.50),
    sum(field_observed_shift_summary$durusdinium__era_2024 >= 0.75),
    sum(field_observed_shift_summary$durusdinium__era_2024 >= 0.90),
    sum(field_observed_shift_summary$durusdinium_change >= 0.25),
    sum(field_observed_shift_summary$durusdinium_change >= 0.50),
    sum(
      field_observed_shift_summary$durusdinium__era_2019_21 < 0.25 &
        field_observed_shift_summary$durusdinium__era_2024 >= 0.50
    ),
    sum(field_observed_shift_summary$hellinger_2019_21_to_2024 >= 0.50)
  ),
  species = c(
    field_observed_species_labels(field_observed_shift_summary$durusdinium__era_2024 >= 0.50),
    field_observed_species_labels(field_observed_shift_summary$durusdinium__era_2024 >= 0.75),
    field_observed_species_labels(field_observed_shift_summary$durusdinium__era_2024 >= 0.90),
    field_observed_species_labels(field_observed_shift_summary$durusdinium_change >= 0.25),
    field_observed_species_labels(field_observed_shift_summary$durusdinium_change >= 0.50),
    field_observed_species_labels(
      field_observed_shift_summary$durusdinium__era_2019_21 < 0.25 &
        field_observed_shift_summary$durusdinium__era_2024 >= 0.50
    ),
    field_observed_species_labels(field_observed_shift_summary$hellinger_2019_21_to_2024 >= 0.50)
  )
)
```

```{r field-observed-genus-shift-plots}
make_field_observed_genus_plot <- function(genus_col, genus_name) {
  plot_data <- across_region_composition |>
    filter(era %in% c("2019-21", "2024")) |>
    transmute(
      host_species_code,
      era,
      n_total,
      genus_proportion = .data[[genus_col]]
    ) |>
    group_by(host_species_code) |>
    filter(all(c("2019-21", "2024") %in% era)) |>
    ungroup()

  species_order <- plot_data |>
    filter(era == "2024") |>
    arrange(genus_proportion) |>
    pull(host_species_code)

  plot_data <- plot_data |>
    mutate(
      host_species_code = factor(host_species_code, levels = species_order),
      era = factor(era, levels = c("2019-21", "2024")),
      genus_count = genus_proportion * n_total,
      genus_adjusted = (genus_count + 0.5) / (n_total + 1),
      genus_se = sqrt(genus_adjusted * (1 - genus_adjusted) / (n_total + 1)),
      genus_lower = pmax(0, genus_proportion - genus_se),
      genus_upper = pmin(1, genus_proportion + genus_se)
    )

  ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = genus_proportion, y = host_species_code)) +
    geom_line(
      aes(group = host_species_code),
      color = "grey70",
      linewidth = 0.6
    ) +
    geom_vline(
      xintercept = c(0.50, 0.75),
      linetype = "dashed",
      color = "grey60",
      linewidth = 0.4
    ) +
    geom_segment(
      aes(
        x = genus_lower,
        xend = genus_upper,
        yend = host_species_code,
        color = era
      ),
      linewidth = 5,
      alpha = 0.22,
      lineend = "round"
    ) +
    geom_point(aes(color = era), size = 2.8, alpha = 0.9) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
      limits = c(0, 1),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.03))
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("2019-21" = "#3B6EA8", "2024" = "#C7533F")) +
    labs(
      x = paste(genus_name, "proportion"),
      y = "Host species",
      color = "Era",
      title = paste("Field-observed", genus_name, "shifts by species"),
      subtitle = "Species-level standardized field summaries; thick transparent bars show approximate +/- 1 SE"
    ) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    )
}
```

## Sample-level dominance and mixing

The genus-proportion plots above summarize the standardized average ITS2 profile
for each species and era. The companion plots below classify individual samples
first, then summarize the standardized fraction of samples in each category.
These plots help distinguish a shift caused by many colonies becoming dominated
by a genus from a shift caused by more mixed communities within colonies.

```{r field-observed-sample-level-summary}
genus_labels <- c(
  A = "Symbiodinium",
  B = "Breviolum",
  C = "Cladocopium",
  D = "Durusdinium",
  G = "Gerakladium"
)

sample_level_metric_cols <- c(
  paste0("dominant_", clades),
  "durusdinium_ge_50",
  "durusdinium_ge_75",
  "durusdinium_ge_90"
)

field_observed_sample_metrics <- sample_clades_retained |>
  mutate(
    dominant_genus = recode(dominant_clade, !!!genus_labels),
    across(all_of(clades), ~ replace_na(.x, 0))
  ) |>
  mutate(
    dominant_A = as.numeric(dominant_clade == "A"),
    dominant_B = as.numeric(dominant_clade == "B"),
    dominant_C = as.numeric(dominant_clade == "C"),
    dominant_D = as.numeric(dominant_clade == "D"),
    dominant_G = as.numeric(dominant_clade == "G"),
    durusdinium_ge_50 = as.numeric(D >= 0.50),
    durusdinium_ge_75 = as.numeric(D >= 0.75),
    durusdinium_ge_90 = as.numeric(D >= 0.90)
  )

weighted_sample_metric_summary <- function(data, metric_cols,
                                           group_cols = c("collection_subregion", "host_species_code"),
                                           min_n = 2, n_bins = 6,
                                           site_col = "collection_site_harmonized",
                                           no_depth_standardization_subregions = "Dry Tortugas") {
  data |>
    group_by(across(all_of(group_cols))) |>
    group_modify(\(.x, .y) {
      df <- .x
      subregion <- if ("collection_subregion" %in% names(.y)) .y$collection_subregion else NA_character_
      skip_depth_standardization <- !is.na(subregion) && subregion %in% no_depth_standardization_subregions
      has_complete_depth <- all(!is.na(df$depth_ft))
      depth_bins <- if (has_complete_depth) make_depth_bins(df$depth_ft, n_bins = n_bins) else factor(rep(NA_character_, nrow(df)))
      use_depth_standardization <- !skip_depth_standardization && has_complete_depth && !all(is.na(depth_bins))
      use_site_standardization <- site_col %in% names(df) && n_distinct(df[[site_col]], na.rm = TRUE) > 1

      if (use_depth_standardization) {
        df <- mutate(df, depth_bin = depth_bins)
      }

      strata_cols <- c(
        if (use_depth_standardization) "depth_bin",
        if (use_site_standardization) site_col
      )

      map_dfr(eras, \(era_i) {
        era_df <- filter(df, era == era_i)
        n_samples <- nrow(era_df)

        if (n_samples < min_n) {
          metric_values <- set_names(rep(NA_real_, length(metric_cols)), metric_cols)
        } else {
          weights <- if (length(strata_cols) > 0) {
            stratification_weights(era_df, df, strata_cols)
          } else {
            rep(1, n_samples)
          }

          if (sum(weights, na.rm = TRUE) == 0) {
            weights <- rep(1, n_samples)
          }

          weights <- weights / sum(weights, na.rm = TRUE)
          metric_values <- map_dbl(metric_cols, \(metric_col) {
            sum(era_df[[metric_col]] * weights, na.rm = TRUE)
          }) |>
            set_names(metric_cols)
        }

        tibble(era = era_i, n = n_samples, !!!as.list(metric_values))
      })
    }) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(era = factor(era, levels = eras))
}

sample_metric_by_region <- weighted_sample_metric_summary(
  field_observed_sample_metrics,
  sample_level_metric_cols,
  min_n = min_n,
  n_bins = 6,
  no_depth_standardization_subregions = "Dry Tortugas"
)

sample_metric_across_region <- sample_metric_by_region |>
  filter(if_any(all_of(sample_level_metric_cols), ~ !is.na(.x))) |>
  summarize(
    n_total = sum(n),
    n_regions = n_distinct(collection_subregion),
    regions_included = paste(sort(unique(collection_subregion)), collapse = "; "),
    across(all_of(sample_level_metric_cols), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .by = c(host_species_code, era)
  )

sample_level_plot_species <- sample_metric_across_region |>
  filter(era %in% c("2019-21", "2024"), !is.na(dominant_D)) |>

durusdinium_sample_prevalence_table <- sample_metric_across_region |>

  select(

  )
```

# Field shifts versus experimental shuffling

The primary comparison asks whether species with stronger experimental
shuffling responses also show larger field-measured shifts in symbiont
composition. Because the experimental data are species-level rather than
subregion-specific, the primary field response is the species-level
site/depth-standardized Hellinger distance from `2019-21` to `2024`. Species
with both Upper Keys and Dry Tortugas estimates are averaged across subregions;
species with one available subregion use that subregion's standardized field
estimate.

The first table is a contrast-level screen: each row correlates the
species-level field shift for one era contrast with the experimental shuffling
coefficient. The `2019-21 to 2024` contrast is the direct comparison to the
field samples collected closest to the experiment.


```{r experimental-field-shift-plot}
estimate_hellinger_response_se <- function(composition, distance_data, n_boot = 1000, seed = 20240630) {
  set.seed(seed)

  map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(distance_data)), \(i) {
    row <- distance_data[i, ]
    p1 <- composition |>
      filter(host_species_code == row$species_code, era == row$era1)
    p2 <- composition |>
      filter(host_species_code == row$species_code, era == row$era2)

    if (
      nrow(p1) != 1 || nrow(p2) != 1 ||
        anyNA(select(p1, all_of(clades))) || anyNA(select(p2, all_of(clades))) ||
        is.na(row$n1) || is.na(row$n2) || row$n1 <= 0 || row$n2 <= 0
    ) {
      return(tibble(species_code = row$species_code, contrast = row$contrast, Hellinger_se = NA_real_))
    }

    p1_vector <- as.numeric(select(p1, all_of(clades)))
    p2_vector <- as.numeric(select(p2, all_of(clades)))
    p1_draws <- t(rmultinom(n_boot, size = row$n1, prob = p1_vector)) / row$n1
    p2_draws <- t(rmultinom(n_boot, size = row$n2, prob = p2_vector)) / row$n2

    tibble(
      species_code = row$species_code,
      contrast = row$contrast,
      Hellinger_se = sd(map2_dbl(
        seq_len(n_boot),
        seq_len(n_boot),
        \(j, k) hellinger_distance(p1_draws[j, ], p2_draws[k, ])
      ))
    )
  })
}

experimental_field_shift_plot_data <- across_region_experimental$distance |>
  filter(
    contrast == "2019-21 to 2024",
    !is.na(mean_shuff_coef),
    !is.na(Hellinger)
  ) |>
  left_join(
    estimate_hellinger_response_se(across_region_composition, across_region_experimental$distance),
    by = c("species_code", "contrast")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    harmonic_field_n = 2 / (1 / n1 + 1 / n2),
    response_weight = 1 / Hellinger_se^2
  )

fit_lm_unweighted <- lm(Hellinger ~ mean_shuff_coef, data = experimental_field_shift_plot_data)
fit_lm_weighted <- lm(
  Hellinger ~ mean_shuff_coef,
  data = experimental_field_shift_plot_data,
  weights = response_weight
)
fit_rlm <- MASS::rlm(Hellinger ~ mean_shuff_coef, data = experimental_field_shift_plot_data)

summarize_lm_shift_model <- function(fit, method, fit_scale = "Raw Hellinger") {
  fit_summary <- summary(fit)
  tibble(
    method = method,
    fit_scale = fit_scale,
    n_species = length(fitted(fit)),
    intercept = coef(fit)[["(Intercept)"]],
    slope = coef(fit)[["mean_shuff_coef"]],
    slope_se = fit_summary$coefficients["mean_shuff_coef", "Std. Error"],
    slope_p = fit_summary$coefficients["mean_shuff_coef", "Pr(>|t|)"],
    r_squared = fit_summary$r.squared
  )
}

summarize_rlm_shift_model <- function(fit, method, fit_scale = "Raw Hellinger") {
  fit_summary <- summary(fit)
  slope <- fit_summary$coefficients["mean_shuff_coef", "Value"]
  slope_se <- fit_summary$coefficients["mean_shuff_coef", "Std. Error"]
  slope_t <- slope / slope_se
  n_species <- length(fitted(fit))
  observed <- model.response(model.frame(fit))

  tibble(
    method = method,
    fit_scale = fit_scale,
    n_species = n_species,
    intercept = coef(fit)[["(Intercept)"]],
    slope = slope,
    slope_se = slope_se,
    slope_p = 2 * pt(abs(slope_t), df = n_species - 2, lower.tail = FALSE),
    r_squared = 1 - sum(resid(fit)^2) / sum((observed - mean(observed))^2)
  )
}

experimental_shift_model_comparison <- bind_rows(
  summarize_lm_shift_model(fit_lm_unweighted, "Unweighted LM"),
  summarize_lm_shift_model(fit_lm_weighted, "Weighted LM (response SE)"),
  summarize_rlm_shift_model(fit_rlm, "Robust regression")
) |>
  mutate(slope_p_formatted = format_sig_p(slope_p))

experimental_shift_model_comparison |>

    digits = 3,
    escape = FALSE,
    caption = "Model comparison for the primary 2019-21 to 2024 field shift versus experimental shuffling coefficient. R-squared is ordinary R-squared for linear models and deviance pseudo-R-squared for fractional-logit models."
  )

experimental_shift_prediction_grid <- tibble(

experimental_shift_model_lines <- bind_rows(
```

## Secondary Durusdinium endpoint comparison

The shuffling-coefficient analysis above focuses on whether experimental
response strength predicts the magnitude of field ITS2 shifts. As a separate
endpoint check, the table and plot below compare the final Durusdinium proportions
measured in the experiment with the species-level 2024 field Durusdinium
proportions.

```{r experimental-clade-d-table}
across_region_experimental$composition_correlations |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 3,
    caption = "Pearson correlation between species-level 2024 ITS2 Durusdinium proportion and experimental Durusdinium proportion"
  )
```

```{r experimental-clade-d-plot}
experimental_clade_d_plot <- across_region_experimental$composition |>
  filter(!is.na(mean_prop_d), !is.na(its2_prop_d_2024)) |>
  mutate(
    field_n = n_its2_2024,
    its2_prop_d_2024_count = its2_prop_d_2024 * n_its2_2024,
    its2_prop_d_2024_adjusted = (its2_prop_d_2024_count + 0.5) / (n_its2_2024 + 1),
    its2_prop_d_2024_se = sqrt(
      its2_prop_d_2024_adjusted * (1 - its2_prop_d_2024_adjusted) / (n_its2_2024 + 1)
    ),
    response_weight = 1 / its2_prop_d_2024_se^2
  )

fit_clade_d_lm_unweighted <- lm(its2_prop_d_2024 ~ mean_prop_d, data = experimental_clade_d_plot)
fit_clade_d_lm_weighted <- lm(
  its2_prop_d_2024 ~ mean_prop_d,
  data = experimental_clade_d_plot,
  weights = response_weight
)
fit_clade_d_rlm <- MASS::rlm(its2_prop_d_2024 ~ mean_prop_d, data = experimental_clade_d_plot)

summarize_clade_d_lm <- function(fit, method) {
  fit_summary <- summary(fit)
  tibble(
    method = method,
    n_species = length(fitted(fit)),
    intercept = coef(fit)[["(Intercept)"]],
    slope = coef(fit)[["mean_prop_d"]],
    slope_se = fit_summary$coefficients["mean_prop_d", "Std. Error"],
    slope_p = fit_summary$coefficients["mean_prop_d", "Pr(>|t|)"],
    r_squared = fit_summary$r.squared
  )
}

summarize_clade_d_rlm <- function(fit, method) {
  fit_summary <- summary(fit)
  slope <- fit_summary$coefficients["mean_prop_d", "Value"]
  slope_se <- fit_summary$coefficients["mean_prop_d", "Std. Error"]
  slope_t <- slope / slope_se
  n_species <- length(fitted(fit))
  observed <- model.response(model.frame(fit))

  tibble(
    method = method,
    n_species = n_species,
    intercept = coef(fit)[["(Intercept)"]],
    slope = slope,
    slope_se = slope_se,
    slope_p = 2 * pt(abs(slope_t), df = n_species - 2, lower.tail = FALSE),
    r_squared = 1 - sum(resid(fit)^2) / sum((observed - mean(observed))^2)
  )
}

experimental_clade_d_model_comparison <- bind_rows(
  summarize_clade_d_lm(fit_clade_d_lm_unweighted, "Unweighted LM"),
  summarize_clade_d_lm(fit_clade_d_lm_weighted, "Weighted LM (response SE)"),
  summarize_clade_d_rlm(fit_clade_d_rlm, "Robust regression")
) |>
  mutate(slope_p_formatted = format_sig_p(slope_p))

experimental_clade_d_model_comparison |>
  select(method, n_species, intercept, slope, slope_se, slope_p = slope_p_formatted, r_squared) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 3,
    escape = FALSE,
    caption = "Model comparison for species-level 2024 ITS2 Durusdinium proportion versus experimental Durusdinium proportion"
  )

experimental_clade_d_prediction_grid <- tibble(
  mean_prop_d = seq(
    min(experimental_clade_d_plot$mean_prop_d),

  )
)

experimental_clade_d_model_lines <- bind_rows(
  experimental_clade_d_prediction_grid |>
    mutate(

    mutate(

experimental_clade_d_plot_out <- ggplot(experimental_clade_d_plot, aes(x = mean_prop_d, y = its2_prop_d_2024)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "grey55") +
```

## Integrated experimental comparison

The polished synthesis treats the shuffling coefficient as the primary
experimental predictor of field composition-shift magnitude, and the Durusdinium
proportion comparison as a secondary endpoint check. The combined figure keeps
the two analyses side-by-side with consistent model display and point-size
weights. Figure lines and 95% confidence bands show weighted fractional-logit
models implemented as quasibinomial GLMs with a logit link and inverse-variance
weights from the field response estimates. For the Hellinger-distance response,
SE is estimated by parametric multinomial bootstrap from the two field
composition estimates; for the 2024 Durusdinium endpoint, SE is approximated from
the 2024 field proportion and sample size using a continuity correction so
observed proportions of exactly 0 or 1 do not receive infinite weight. This is a quasi-likelihood mean model for bounded
responses rather than a literal binomial sampling model, which is appropriate
here because both field responses are continuous species-level summaries rather
than counts of successes and failures. The logit link keeps predicted means and
confidence bands inside the 0-1 response scale. Linear and robust fits are
retained as sensitivity checks in the table below.

```{r integrated-experimental-model-table}
fit_shift_fractional_logit_weighted <- glm(
  Hellinger ~ mean_shuff_coef,
  data = experimental_field_shift_plot_data,
  weights = response_weight,
  family = quasibinomial(link = "logit")
)

fit_clade_d_fractional_logit_weighted <- glm(
  its2_prop_d_2024 ~ mean_prop_d,
  data = experimental_clade_d_plot,
  weights = response_weight,
  family = quasibinomial(link = "logit")
)

summarize_weighted_fractional_logit <- function(fit, method, slope_name) {
  fit_summary <- summary(fit)
  p_column <- grep("^Pr", colnames(fit_summary$coefficients), value = TRUE)

  tibble(
    method = method,
    model_family = "Quasibinomial GLM, logit link",
    n_species = length(fitted(fit)),
    intercept = coef(fit)[["(Intercept)"]],
    slope = coef(fit)[[slope_name]],
    slope_se = fit_summary$coefficients[slope_name, "Std. Error"],
    slope_p = fit_summary$coefficients[slope_name, p_column],
    r_squared = 1 - fit$deviance / fit$null.deviance
  ) |>
    mutate(slope_p_formatted = format_sig_p(slope_p))
}

integrated_experimental_model_comparison <- bind_rows(
  summarize_weighted_fractional_logit(
    fit_shift_fractional_logit_weighted,
    "Weighted fractional logit (response SE)",
    "mean_shuff_coef"
  ) |>
    mutate(
      endpoint = "Composition-shift magnitude",
      predictor = "Experimental shuffling coefficient",
      response = "2019-21 to 2024 Hellinger distance",
      model_role = "Displayed bounded model"
    ),
  experimental_shift_model_comparison |>
    mutate(
      endpoint = "Composition-shift magnitude",
      predictor = "Experimental shuffling coefficient",
      response = "2019-21 to 2024 Hellinger distance",
      model_family = "Gaussian/robust linear",
      model_role = "Sensitivity check"
    ),
  summarize_weighted_fractional_logit(
    fit_clade_d_fractional_logit_weighted,
    "Weighted fractional logit (response SE)",
    "mean_prop_d"
  ) |>
    mutate(
      endpoint = "Durusdinium endpoint",
      predictor = "Experimental Durusdinium proportion",
      response = "2024 ITS2 Durusdinium proportion",
      model_role = "Displayed bounded model"
    ),
  experimental_clade_d_model_comparison |>
    mutate(
      endpoint = "Durusdinium endpoint",
      predictor = "Experimental Durusdinium proportion",
      response = "2024 ITS2 Durusdinium proportion",
      model_family = "Gaussian/robust linear",
      model_role = "Sensitivity check"
    )
) |>
  mutate(
    endpoint = factor(endpoint, levels = c("Composition-shift magnitude", "Durusdinium endpoint")),
    model_role = factor(model_role, levels = c("Displayed bounded model", "Sensitivity check")),
    method = factor(
      method,
      levels = c(
        "Weighted fractional logit (response SE)",
        "Unweighted LM",
        "Weighted LM (response SE)",
        "Robust regression"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  select(
    endpoint, predictor, response, model_role, method, model_family, n_species,
    intercept, slope, slope_se, slope_p = slope_p_formatted, r_squared
  )

integrated_experimental_model_comparison |>
  arrange(endpoint, model_role, method) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 3,
    escape = FALSE,
    caption = "Integrated experimental-to-field model comparison. Quasibinomial/fractional-logit models are displayed in the figure because the response variables are bounded from 0 to 1; linear and robust fits are sensitivity checks."
  )
```

```{r integrated-experimental-leave-one-out}
summarize_fractional_logit_fit <- function(fit, slope_name) {
  fit_summary <- summary(fit)
  p_column <- grep("^Pr", colnames(fit_summary$coefficients), value = TRUE)

  tibble(
    n_species = length(fitted(fit)),
    slope = coef(fit)[[slope_name]],
    slope_se = fit_summary$coefficients[slope_name, "Std. Error"],
    slope_p = fit_summary$coefficients[slope_name, p_column],
    pseudo_r2 = 1 - fit$deviance / fit$null.deviance
  )
}

leave_one_species_out_fractional_logit <- function(data, endpoint, response_col, predictor_col, weight_col) {
  formula <- reformulate(predictor_col, response_col)
  data <- mutate(data, .model_weight = .data[[weight_col]])
  full_fit <- glm(
    formula,
    data = data,
    weights = .model_weight,
    family = quasibinomial(link = "logit")
  )

  bind_rows(
    summarize_fractional_logit_fit(full_fit, predictor_col) |>
      mutate(endpoint = endpoint, omitted_species = "None"),
    map_dfr(sort(unique(data$species_code)), \(species_i) {
      fit_data <- filter(data, species_code != species_i)
      fit <- glm(
        formula,
        data = fit_data,
        weights = .model_weight,
        family = quasibinomial(link = "logit")
      )

      summarize_fractional_logit_fit(fit, predictor_col) |>
        mutate(endpoint = endpoint, omitted_species = species_i)
    })
  ) |>
    mutate(
      endpoint = factor(endpoint, levels = c("Composition-shift magnitude", "Durusdinium endpoint")),
      slope_p_formatted = format_sig_p(slope_p)
    )
}

integrated_experimental_leave_one_out <- bind_rows(
  leave_one_species_out_fractional_logit(
    experimental_field_shift_plot_data,
    endpoint = "Composition-shift magnitude",
    response_col = "Hellinger",
    predictor_col = "mean_shuff_coef",
    weight_col = "response_weight"
  ),
  leave_one_species_out_fractional_logit(
    experimental_clade_d_plot,
    endpoint = "Durusdinium endpoint",
    response_col = "its2_prop_d_2024",
    predictor_col = "mean_prop_d",
    weight_col = "response_weight"
  )
)

integrated_experimental_leave_one_out |>
  arrange(endpoint, omitted_species) |>
  select(endpoint, omitted_species, n_species, slope, slope_se, slope_p = slope_p_formatted, pseudo_r2) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 3,
    escape = FALSE,
    caption = "Leave-one-species-out sensitivity for the displayed response-SE weighted quasibinomial models"
  )

leave_one_out_reference <- integrated_experimental_leave_one_out |>
  filter(omitted_species == "None") |>
  select(endpoint, full_slope = slope)

leave_one_out_plot_data <- integrated_experimental_leave_one_out |>
  filter(omitted_species != "None") |>
  left_join(leave_one_out_reference, by = "endpoint") |>
  mutate(
    slope_lwr = slope - 1.96 * slope_se,
    slope_upr = slope + 1.96 * slope_se,
    omitted_species = fct_reorder(omitted_species, slope)
  )

leave_one_out_plot <- ggplot(
  leave_one_out_plot_data,
  aes(x = omitted_species, y = slope)
) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = full_slope), color = "#1f78b4", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = slope_lwr, ymax = slope_upr), width = 0, alpha = 0.55) +
  geom_point(size = 2.7, alpha = 0.85) +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~ endpoint, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    x = "Species omitted",
    y = "Quasibinomial slope estimate",
    caption = "Blue line is the full-data slope; intervals are approximate +/- 1.96 SE from each leave-one-out fit."
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "grey30", hjust = 0)
  )
```

```{r integrated-experimental-comparison-figure}
predict_fractional_logit_ci <- function(fit, newdata) {
  prediction <- predict(fit, newdata = newdata, type = "link", se.fit = TRUE)
  critical_value <- qt(0.975, df = fit$df.residual)

  bind_cols(
    newdata,
    tibble(
      fit = plogis(prediction$fit),
      lwr = plogis(prediction$fit - critical_value * prediction$se.fit),
      upr = plogis(prediction$fit + critical_value * prediction$se.fit)
    )
  )
}

  experimental_shift_prediction_grid
)
```

```{r field-response-se-diagnostic}
    min.segment.length = 0,
    segment.color = "grey65",
    segment.size = 0.25,
    box.padding = 0.25,
    point.padding = 0.22,
    max.overlaps = Inf
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ endpoint, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    x = "Field sample support",
    y = "Field response SE",
    caption = "Hellinger support is the harmonic mean of the two era sample sizes; Durusdinium support is the 2024 ITS2 sample size."
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "grey30", hjust = 0)
  )

field_response_se_diagnostic_plot

ggsave(
  "outputs/figures/field_response_se_vs_sample_support.png",
  field_response_se_diagnostic_plot,
  width = 9,
  height = 4.5,
  dpi = 300
)
```

# Across-region synthesis

This section combines Upper Keys and Dry Tortugas into one species-level view.
The inputs are the region-level compositions above: Upper Keys is standardized
by site and depth where possible, and Dry Tortugas is standardized by site but
not by depth because depth data are incomplete.

Regions are weighted equally when both regions are available for a species and
era. This is intended as an across-region biological synthesis rather than a
sample-size-weighted summary dominated by the region with more samples.

```{r across-region-composition}
across_region_composition |>
  arrange(host_species_code, era) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r across-region-composition-plot}
across_region_composition_long <- across_region_composition |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(clades), names_to = "clade", values_to = "proportion") |>
  filter(!is.na(proportion))

across_region_composition_plot <- ggplot(
  across_region_composition_long,
  aes(x = era, y = proportion, fill = clade)
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8, color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ host_species_code) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Across-region symbiont composition",
    fill = "Clade"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

across_region_composition_plot

ggsave(
  "outputs/figures/across_region_species_composition.png",
  across_region_composition_plot,
  width = 11,
  height = 7,
  dpi = 300
)
```
